The same process by which vegetable matter is turned to flesh in plants and animals, is called in Latin animalization.

The notion of ‘vegetablizing’ and ‘animalizing’ elements to be assimilated to animals' bodies was also used metaphorically by scientists.

Plants were thought to be capable of converting the elements, and hence of ‘vegetablizing’ water, which was thus ‘de-animated’. They were also thought of as able to ‘animalise’ the elements, that is to say, to transform them into animal matter.
